subject: (simple) Mixture model - why does not work as classification algorithm?

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: (simple) Mixture model - why does not work as classification algorithm?
parts:
Hello,

I made work this simple mixture model: 


Given:

1) the data

2) the known central normal distribution (mu=0, sd=known)

3) the unknown side normal distributions with mu_right = - mu_left  


I am able to identify the three distributions and their proportions.



 my.in <-
 list(

   N = 100L,

    y = c(rnorm(60, 0, 0.56), rnorm(20, 1.2, 0.5), rnorm(20, -1.2, 0.5)),

    mu_nn = 0.0102204341046514,

    sigma_nn = 0.564371245496221,

    alpha = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)

 )


mod <- "

data {

 int<lower=1> N; // number of data points

 real y[N]; // observations

 real mu_nn;

 real sigma_nn;

}

parameters {

 simplex[3] theta; // mixing proportions

 real<lower=0> mu_up;

 real<lower=0> sigma;

}

transformed parameters{

 real<upper=0> mu_down;

 mu_down <- -mu_up;

}

model {

 real ps[2]; // temp for log component densities

 vector[3] log_theta;//For speed up

 log_theta <- log(theta); //For speed up


  sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5);

 mu_up ~ normal(0,10);


  for (n in 1:N) {

   if(y[n] > 0) ps[1] <- log_theta[1] + normal_log(y[n],mu_up,sigma); //either is positive or negative

   else ps[1] <- log_theta[2] + normal_log(y[n],mu_down,sigma); //either is positive or negative

   ps[2] <- log_theta[3] + normal_log(y[n],mu_nn,sigma_nn); //for central distribution


    increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps));

 }

}

"


fit <- stan(model_code=mod, data=my.in)




$summary

So far so good.


NOW...



I actually want to have a table (Dirichlet?) that states the probability of each observation to belong to which distribution. For example y == 2 must have probability ~ 1 to belong to the right distribution.


For achieving this I created the following code, that instead of theta being a simplex with length 3, would be a table with a row per observation -> simplex[3]  theta[N].

In my mind the ration of sums of the columns of theta should reflect 0.2, 0.2, 0.6 proportions of the previous model.



mod <- "

data {

  int<lower=1> N; // number of data points
  real y[N]; // observations
  real mu_nn;
  real sigma_nn;
}

parameters {
  simplex[3] theta[N]; // mixing proportions
  real<lower=0> mu_up;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}

transformed parameters{
  real<upper=0> mu_down;
  mu_down <- -mu_up;
}

model {
  real ps[2]; // temp for log component densities
  vector[3] log_theta[N];//For speed up
  for(n in 1:N) log_theta[n] <- log(theta[n]); //For speed up

  sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  mu_up ~ normal(0,10);

  for (n in 1:N) {

    if(y[n] > 0) ps[1] <- log_theta[n,1] + normal_log(y[n],mu_up,sigma); //either is positive or negative
    else ps[1] <- log_theta[n,2] + normal_log(y[n],mu_down,sigma); //either is positive or negative
    ps[2] <- log_theta[n,3] + normal_log(y[n],mu_nn,sigma_nn); //for central distribution

    increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps));

  }
}
"

fit <- stan(model_code=mod, data=my.in)

fit.theta <- as.data.frame(extract(fit, pars="theta"))
doc.topic <- do.call("rbind", lapply(colnames(fit.theta), function(x) strsplit(x, ".", fixed=T)[[1]]))
fit.theta <- data.frame(gene = as.numeric(doc.topic[,2]), topic = as.factor(doc.topic[,3]),  mean = colMeans(fit.theta))

colMeans(dcast(fit.theta, gene~topic));




      gene          1          2          3 
50.5000000  0.3311502  0.3200185  0.3488313

the three mean of proportions are different from the expected 0.2, 0.2, 0.6



Am I missing something?

Thanks a lot.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] (simple) Mixture model - why does not work as classification algorithm?
parts:
Sorry for the long delay. I'm just catching up with mail
nobody answered.

The problem you're having at the end is probably due to label switching.
Try rerunning with chains=1 and see if the problem goes away.
There's a discussion in the problematic posteriors section of
the manual.

And I would not try to get clever with the mixing proportions
the way you are looking at y < 0 and y > 0. The model will
sort this out, so ps should be of length 3 and it should be
just as in the manual, replacing

> if(y[n] > 0) ps[1] <- log_theta[1] + normal_log(y[n],mu_up,sigma); //either is positive or negative
>
> else ps[1] <- log_theta[2] + normal_log(y[n],mu_down,sigma); //either is positive or negative
>
> ps[2] <- log_theta[3] + normal_log(y[n],mu_nn,sigma_nn); //for central distribution



ps[1] <- log_theta[1] + normal_log(y[n], mu_up, sigma);

ps[2] <- log_theta[2] + normal_log(y[n], mu_down, sigma);
ps[3] <- log_theta[3] + normal_log(y[n], mu_nn, sigma_nn);



-Bob




- Bob
